incumbent.name: Sean Fagan
incumbent.summary: Sean Fagan, a Republican, has been La Porte County prosecutor since defeating then-Prosecutor John Lake in November 2022; he lost the May 2026 Republican primary to Chuck Watterson, IV, who had served as his chief deputy, so the seat will change hands {lp_2022_general}  {lp_2026_primary}.
record: November 8, 2022: Defeated incumbent Democrat John Lake, 16,350 votes (51.46%) to 15,425 (48.54%), in election-night results {lp_2022_general}.
May 5, 2026: Lost the Republican primary to Watterson, 41.45% to 58.55%, in unofficial results {lp_2026_primary} {wsbt_primary}.

race_context: The 32nd Judicial Circuit prosecutor handles criminal cases in La Porte County. The race is effectively an open seat: incumbent Sean Fagan lost the May 2026 Republican primary {lp_2026_primary}.

Republican primary (May 5, 2026, unofficial, 92 of 92 precincts): Watterson 3,631 votes (58.55%), Fagan 2,571 (41.45%). Lake was unopposed in the Democratic primary with 4,823 votes {lp_2026_primary}.
No general-election forum or debate between Lake and Watterson was found in available coverage.

candidates.summary: Chuck Watterson, IV is a criminal trial attorney who served as a deputy prosecutor under John Lake and as chief deputy prosecutor under Sean Fagan; he won the 2026 Republican nomination over Fagan  {wsbt_primary}.
background: Described in March 2026 by the Herald-Dispatch as currently working as a defense attorney; WSBT described him in May 2026 as the county's chief deputy prosecuting attorney {wsbt_primary}.
path_to_ballot: Won the May 5, 2026 Republican primary over incumbent Sean Fagan with 58.55% of the vote in unofficial results {lp_2026_primary} {wsbt_primary}.
plans: No detailed plans for the office were found in available coverage.
endorsements_finance: Pre-primary report (Jan. 1–Apr. 10, 2026): $8,861.90 raised, $7,046.66 spent, $1,815.24 cash on hand and $1,000 in debts {lp_cf_watterson}.
gaps: Sources conflict on his current job: the Herald-Dispatch (March 2026) said he works as a defense attorney, while WSBT (May 2026) called him chief deputy prosecuting attorney; not resolved.
Other forum remarks (on leading deputies and dealing with media and victims' families) could not be reliably attributed between candidates in the encoded article text and were not used.
No campaign website, questionnaire or general-election statements found; positions on backlogs, diversion, violent crime, juvenile justice and victims' services not found.
Later campaign-finance reports were not reviewed.
The La Porte County Herald-Dispatch's candidate forum coverage is behind a paywall and was not used.

candidates.summary: John Lake is a former La Porte County prosecutor (elected 2018, defeated 2022) with about 35 years of legal experience who was described in March 2026 as a St. Joseph County deputy prosecutor  {lp_2022_general}.
background: La Porte County prosecutor for one term after his 2018 election; lost re-election to Fagan in 2022  {lp_2022_general}.
